entries.title: Seed Dispersal and Sapling Growth Field
entries.description: A 3D clearing with a few tall parent trees that periodically eject small glowing seed spheres which float, drift with a light wind, land on a textured ground plane, attach to soil patches, and slowly grow into semi-transparent green cylinders that thicken, branch upward, and change color as they mature, with labels showing age and height.

entries.title: Competing Trees for Light and Space
entries.description: A grid of young tree cylinders that grow upward and outward while semi-transparent yellow light beams from above are blocked by taller neighbors, causing shaded trees to slow, bend toward gaps, or stop growing, with dynamic height meters and color shifts to show competition intensity.
entries.seed: Competing Trees for Light and Space: A grid of young tree cylinders that grow upward and outward while semi-transparent yellow light beams from above are blocked by taller neighbors, causing shaded trees to slow, bend toward gaps, or stop growing, with dynamic height meters and color shifts to show competition intensity.

entries.title: Forest Succession After a Fire Front
entries.description: A forest scene where a moving semi-transparent red “fire wall” passes through and turns trees blackened and leafless, followed over time by sprouting green seedling particles that appear around burned trunks, grow, and eventually replace them, with a timeline slider and labels for pioneer vs. mature species.

entries.title: Root Network Underground Expansion
entries.description: Trees above a semi-transparent soil box send branching root tubes downward and outward, which grow, split, and sometimes collide or wrap around rocks, with roots changing color where they overlap and a toggle to hide the surface canopy and reveal the glowing underground network.

entries.title: Seasonal Forest Canopy Cycle
entries.description: A stand of trees with static trunks but dynamic canopy spheres that grow, change color from pale green to deep green, then yellow/orange, then shrink and detach as leaf particles that drift to the ground and form a thin, growing leaf layer, with a “season” dial controlling speed.

entries.title: Rainfall, Soil Moisture, and Tree Growth Feedback
entries.description: A light-background scene where blue raindrop particles fall onto a gently sloped, textured terrain, seep into a semi-transparent soil volume, and raise local water level bars near each tree, which then grow faster or slower depending on water bars, with evaporating mist particles above drier zones.

entries.title: Canopy Gap Formation and Regeneration
entries.description: A dense canopy of overlapping green domes representing tree crowns where random trees “fall” (trunks tilt, detach, and slowly collapse to the ground), opening bright circular light patches that trigger faster growth and branching of nearby saplings in the gap, with arrows showing light direction.

entries.title: Mycorrhizal Fungal Network and Resource Transfer
entries.description: Multiple tree trunks connected underground by thin glowing tubes that branch like fungal hyphae, where colored resource pulses (e.g., blue for water, orange for sugars) travel along the tubes between trees, with labels showing donors and receivers and the network thickening where traffic is heavier.

entries.title: Forest Edge vs. Interior Growth Gradient
entries.description: A rectangular forest block where trees along the bright, open edges grow taller and bushier, while interior trees grow slower and more slender, with a movable “sun” light source and semi-transparent yellow light gradients that fade toward the center, plus on-hover labels with growth rates.

entries.title: Slope, Erosion, and Tree Stability
entries.description: A sloped terrain with scattered trees whose roots (semi-transparent cones) grow into the hillside; when heavy rain bursts of blue particles hit, soil cubes can detach and slide downslope, destabilizing trees whose roots are too shallow, causing them to tilt, uproot, and slide while others remain anchored.

entries.title: Patchy Forest Regeneration on a Checkerboard Landscape
entries.description: A checkerboard of soil quality tiles (green = fertile, brown = poor, gray = rock) where seeds rain down from above and only germinate on suitable tiles, then grow into trees that cast circular shadow disks and spread more seeds preferentially into nearby fertile tiles, with each tile labeled and color-coded.

entries.title: Invasive Species Overtaking a Young Forest
entries.description: Native saplings (soft green cylinders) grow slowly across a clearing while an invasive shrub species (bright red, bushy shapes) rapidly spreads by sending out horizontally expanding clones that attach to ground patches, crowd natives, and dim their color as they lose resources, with a live count display.

entries.title: Vertical Forest Stratification: Understory to Emergent Trees
entries.description: Layers of plants from low ferns and shrubs up to mid-story trees and emergent giants, where each layer grows at different speeds and reacts to light penetration from above, with semi-transparent planes indicating strata heights and cross-section mode to watch vertical growth and branching patterns.

entries.title: Wind-Driven Tree Sway and Branch Breakage
entries.description: A grove of tall trees with flexible segmented trunks and branches that bend, sway, and sometimes snap off as invisible wind strength (shown by moving arrow fields) increases and pulses, with broken branches falling, bouncing, and leaving scars highlighted in red on trunks.

entries.title: Urban Tree Planting and Growth Along a Street
entries.description: A straight road with buildings as stationary boxes and newly planted small trees in sidewalk pits that gradually grow crowns which extend toward light gaps between buildings, avoiding collisions with building faces and occasional passing vehicles, with labels tracking each tree’s height and crown width.

entries.title: Forest Carbon Stock Accumulation Over Time
entries.description: A forest plot where each tree grows in diameter and height while a floating transparent bar or sphere above it fills with darker green to represent accumulated carbon, and a large aggregated carbon meter on the side rises as the forest matures, with dead trees turning gray and losing part of their carbon.

entries.description: A zoomed-in single twig that lengthens over time with buds (small bumps) that swell, split open, and unfold into semi-transparent leaves that rotate to face a moving light source, with faint green growth rings appearing along the twig as it elongates.

entries.description: A winding blue river through a valley where tree seeds preferentially germinate near the moist banks, creating dense green bands that thicken and stretch outward over time, with occasional flood events causing water level to rise, uprooting some trees and depositing new seeds downstream.

entries.description: A mountain cross-section where temperature and oxygen gradients are shown as colored bands, with trees growing and creeping higher over time as climate warms (bands shift upward), while above the tree line only small shrubs appear and disappear, with a slider controlling warming rate.
